html:
The Guamares were a Chichimec people of the Bajío and the highlands of today's Guanajuato state in central Mexico. Spanish writers of the 1500s called them the bravest and most warlike of the Chichimec nations. They lived mainly by hunting and gathering.

After silver was found at Zacatecas in 1546, and later at Guanajuato, Spanish wagon roads ran through their land. The Guamares joined the Guachichil, Zacateco and others in the Chichimeca War, which lasted from about 1550 to 1590. New Spain ended it by buying peace with food and clothing and by settling Christian Tlaxcalan colonists among them. The Guamares were absorbed and vanished as a separate people.
